Italian Gaming Group Lottomatica to Merge With Spain's Cirsa
By Dominic Chopping
Gaming groups Lottomatica and Cirsa Enterprises have agreed to an all-share merger deal that will see the combined group retain a listing in both Italy and Spain.
Milan-listed Lottomatica said that Wednesday's deal will see shareholders of Barcelona-based Cirsa receive 0.668 newly issued Lottomatica shares for each share held.
Lottomatica will continue as the surviving entity.

"The proposed combination will create a global leading sports betting and gaming player, with number one positions in Italy and Spain, and leading presence in other high-growth markets," the companies said in a joint statement.

They said the deal will create the second largest listed gaming and sports betting operator globally, with pro forma adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization of around 2 billion euros ($2.32 billion) in the year to June 30.
The companies also said that the combined group will have an attractive shareholder-return profile, online growth opportunities and yield around 115 million euros of pre-tax cash annual synergies.
Cirsa's majority shareholder, LHMC Midco, a company controlled by Blackstone, has also agreed the deal.

Before implementing the merger, Cirsa will distribute to its shareholders an extraordinary dividend of 262 million euros, or 1.56 euros per share. Upon completion, Lottomatica intends to propose shareholders of the combined company a capital return of 744 million euros.
